stem: A developer notices a bug only reproduces intermittently and can't easily pin down why. Given the general principle discussed for controlled comparisons elsewhere, what debugging practice most directly helps isolate the actual triggering condition?
explanation: Systematically varying one factor at a time (holding all other request parameters/inputs constant while changing just one specific variable, such as a particular input characteristic or a specific parameter value) while observing whether the bug reproduces connects directly to the same controlled-comparison/isolate-one-variable principle discussed for A/B testing and model tier comparisons elsewhere, methodically narrowing down which specific factor actually triggers the intermittent behavior rather than changing multiple things at once and being unable to attribute the result to any specific cause.
reference: Controlled, one-variable-at-a-time isolation for intermittent bugs

choices.text: Systematically varying one factor at a time while holding everything else constant.
choices.reasoning: Correct: this connects the general controlled-comparison/isolate-one-variable principle (discussed for A/B testing, model tier comparisons) directly to this debugging scenario, systematically changing one thing at a time is what actually lets a developer attribute the intermittent behavior to a specific cause.

choices.text: There is no systematic way to debug an intermittent issue; a developer must simply guess randomly until the bug happens to reproduce.
choices.reasoning: Incorrect: this dismisses a real, systematic debugging methodology (controlled, one-variable-at-a-time isolation) that directly applies to exactly this kind of intermittent-bug diagnosis.

choices.text: This can only be diagnosed by switching to a different model tier.
choices.reasoning: Incorrect: this is a debugging methodology (controlled variable isolation), not something addressed by changing which model tier is used.

choices.text: This practice only applies if the bug involves extended thinking.
choices.reasoning: Incorrect: the controlled, one-variable-at-a-time isolation technique applies to debugging intermittent issues generally, independent of whether extended thinking happens to be involved.

stem: Truly final question for this domain and this certification: a developer has built a robust evaluation and debugging practice (golden datasets, regression tests, isolated component testing, systematic A/B comparisons). What ongoing discipline does maintaining this practice require, connecting to the theme of ongoing vigilance discussed across multiple domains?
explanation: Maintaining this practice requires ongoing attention and periodic revisiting, not a one-time setup, connecting to the same recurring theme discussed across cost monitoring, jailbreak resistance, and permission review elsewhere in this certification: datasets need updating as usage evolves, regression suites need new cases added as new issues are found and fixed, and comparison practices need to keep pace as the application and underlying models themselves continue to change over time, reinforcing that sound evaluation practice is a continuous discipline, not a completed, one-time project.
reference: Ongoing vigilance as the final connecting theme for evaluation practice

choices.text: Ongoing attention and periodic revisiting, not a one-time setup, connecting to the same recurring theme discussed for cost monitoring, jailbreak resistance, and permission review.
choices.reasoning: Correct: this correctly connects the final capstone of this domain to the same ongoing-vigilance theme that has recurred across multiple other domains in this certification, reinforcing that sound practice, evaluation included, is a continuous discipline rather than a completed, one-time project.

choices.text: Once established, a robust evaluation and debugging practice requires no further attention or updates, ever, regardless of how the application or usage evolves.
choices.reasoning: Incorrect: this treats an evolving practice as permanently fixed and complete, contradicting the same ongoing-vigilance theme established repeatedly throughout this certification for analogous practices.

choices.text: This ongoing discipline can only be maintained by switching to a different model tier periodically.
choices.reasoning: Incorrect: maintaining an evaluation/debugging practice is about ongoing attention to datasets, tests, and comparisons, not primarily a function of periodically changing model tier.

choices.text: This discipline only applies if the application uses the Batches API.
choices.reasoning: Incorrect: the need for ongoing evaluation/debugging discipline applies broadly to any application, independent of which processing mode is used.
